name: Mastodon (mastodon.social as the example instance)

why.quote: Whoever owns the Content retains ownership.
why.page: https://mastodon.social/api/v1/instance/terms_of_service (Terms for registered users of mastodon.social, effective 2026-08-31; the same text is at https://mastodon.social/terms-of-service)
why.basis: the instance's terms (content stays its owner's; the licence given to the operator covers making content available "via one or more APIs for application access, via RSS") and https://mastodon.social/robots.txt, whose group for User-agent: * disallows only /media_proxy/, /interact/ and /api/v1/instance/domain_blocks

interface: Public REST API and per-account RSS/Atom (.rss) on the instance; each instance sets its own rules.
notes: Read 18 Nov 2026 by data.b.collector@. Other instances (e.g. masto.pt) have their own terms, not yet read: add each instance here before listing an account on it. Named AI-training agents are disallowed by robots.txt: we are a news data collector, not an AI-training crawler, and store no text.
how: Mastodon public instance API, without credentials: /api/v1/accounts/lookup and /api/v1/accounts/:id/statuses (exclude_replies) on the instance of each listed organisation account (register/social-accounts.json; none yet), with our named user agent and 2.5 s between requests. Post text read in memory only; never stored. Each instance sets its own terms: the collector reads only instances whose terms were read, and mastodon.social's are the ones read so far.
